Tap Font size and style (critical)
Adjust size (and optionally bold) on that screen (critical)
For darker text: Settings > Accessibility > Visibility enhancements > turn on high contrast fonts (adds an outline to text)
unsupported_claims: 'You can also choose to make it bold, which makes the letters darker and thicker' -> the page does not say bold makes letters darker; the page's option for stronger text is high contrast fonts
reasons: User asked for larger AND darker text. The only page-supported darker/stronger option (high contrast fonts) is missing, and the 'darker' claim for bold is not on the page.
fix: Keep steps 1-4. Remove 'which makes the letters darker and thicker'; say only 'You can also turn on bold on that screen.' Then add a short second part for darker text: 'To make the words stand out more, open Settings, tap Accessibility, tap Visibility enhancements, and turn on the switch next to high contrast fonts. This adds an outline around all the text so it stands out from the background.' Keep the hedge about menu names.

required_actions: Check whether Gmail is down (Google Workspace Status Dashboard)
Update browser to latest version (critical)
Try another browser
Turn off extensions / uninstall computer apps one at a time, or use incognito/private window
Clear browser cache and cookies, then open Gmail again
reasons: Drops the page's extensions/incognito step and the status check; step 4 'Clear your browser's saved website data (called cache and cookies)' gives no starting point, so a low-confidence user cannot act on it (S4). Reply also never asks which browser is used, so the how-to cannot be specific.
fix: Add as step 1: 'Check whether Gmail is down: look at the Google Workspace Status Dashboard.' Add after the different-browser step: 'Turn off any browser extensions one at a time, opening Gmail again after each one. You can also try a private (incognito) window.' For the cache step, either keep it as 'Clear your browser's cache and cookies, then open Gmail again' and add the second official Google source https://support.google.com/accounts/answer/32050 (Chrome: clear cache and cookies) with its exact menu path, or end with one short question asking which browser they use. Keep one action per step.

reasons: User said 'I tried turning it off and on' (already restarted); step 3 'Restart your computer and open Gmail again' repeats what she did. Page's clear cache and cookies and extensions steps are left out while the repeat is included.

Optionally add 'Turn off browser extensions one at a time, opening Gmail after each.' Keep update browser, different browser, and the Wi-Fi off and on step.

reasons: Windows 11 user, but the page's first step for Windows 11 (open the Get Help app and run the printer troubleshooter) is missing. Step 4 bundles 'look for a button' and 'use it to make sure wireless is on'; the extra 'make sure your laptop is online' (step 6) is not on the page.
fix: Add a first step: 'Open the **Get Help** app and run the printer troubleshooter. It checks the printer and tries to fix most problems.' Reword step 4 to 'Make sure the printer's wireless is on. Many printers have a button with a blue wireless icon.' Delete step 6 ('make sure your laptop is online') or fold it into the same-network step. Keep the same-network step with the extender explanation.

reasons: Missing the final Next after 'Do not share this printer' (step 9 ends at the sharing choice, step 10 jumps to the test page) and the driver-source choice (Windows Update/Have Disk). Steps 1, 2 and 9 pack several clicks together; ten steps in one reply is long for the user.
fix: Step 8: 'Choose your printer's maker and model. If asked, choose **Windows Update** so Windows finds the driver, then click **Next**.' Split step 9 into 'Type a name for the printer and click **Next**.' and 'Choose **Do not share this printer**, then click **Next**.' Keep the 'Print a test page, then Finish' step. If length exceeds the cap, drop the Add manually branch steps 5-9 into one line pointing to the same page.
